status_summary: On 2026-01-22 NIH issued notice NOT-OD-26-028, effective immediately, ending use of NIH funds for research on human fetal tissue from elective abortions, in both the intramural program and extramural research (applying to proposals under solicitations issued after that date; existing awards may redirect funds to other work). This goes beyond the Mandate's request to restore an ethics advisory board review, which the notices do not mention. On 2026-01-23 NIH paused review of applications to add new human embryonic stem cell lines to its registry and opened a request for information (comments closed 2026-04-24) on replacing such cells with alternatives; the registry's existing 503 lines remain usable, so the registry has not been ended. No statutory prohibition, National Council on Bioethics, or dedicated funding plan for alternatives was found.

timeline.event: Context before the tracking window: a 2019 policy required ethics advisory board review of extramural fetal tissue proposals; the Biden administration reversed these restrictions in 2021 (year only given in source; first of year used) and said no new board would be convened.

NIH issues NOT-OD-26-028, NIH Policy on Research Involving Human Fetal Tissue: NIH funds may not be used for research on human fetal tissue from elective abortions, intramural or extramural, effective the same day. Fetal tissue from miscarriage or stillbirth remains eligible under earlier notices.

NIH news release announces the policy and says it will seek public comment on whether newer biotechnologies could reduce or replace reliance on human embryonic stem cells; it cites organoids, tissue chips, and computational methods as alternatives.

NIH issues NOT-OD-26-031: it pauses review and approval of applications to add new lines to the NIH Human Embryonic Stem Cell Registry (503 approved lines; last addition December 2023) and requests public input on where alternatives could replace human embryonic stem cells. Lines already listed remain usable in NIH-funded research.

Comment period on the human embryonic stem cell request for information closes; FASEB reports submitting comments on 2026-04-14 urging NIH to lift the registry pause. No later NIH action on embryonic stem cell funding or the registry was found.

title: End NIH funding of abortion-derived fetal tissue and embryonic stem cell research
uncertainties: Searches covered NIH Guide notices, NIH news releases, law-firm alerts, a FASEB tracker, and Congress/bioethics-council terms. Not found: any NIH action on the embryonic stem cell registry after the 2026-04-24 comment deadline (a later decision could change the stage), any National Council on Bioethics, any appropriations rider or enacted statute on fetal tissue in the 119th Congress, or any lawsuit against the policy. The Ropes & Gray alert is dated by month only (January 2026, first of month used). The 2021 context event uses year only.
